name: LaunchDarkly
description: LaunchDarkly feature flags: projects and environments, flags with state and evaluation status, segments, metrics and experiments, the audit log, members and teams. Create flags and segments, turn flags on or off and change targeting with semantic patches.
instructions:
## LaunchDarkly
This connector works with **LaunchDarkly** feature management through its REST API (`https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2`, API version 20240415): projects and environments, feature flags with their state and evaluation status, segments, metrics and experiments, the audit log, members and teams. It can create flags and segments, turn flags on or off, and change targeting with semantic patch instructions.

**Setup (2 minutes)**
1. In LaunchDarkly open **Organization settings, Authorization** (https://app.launchdarkly.com/settings/authorization) and create an access token. For reading choose the **Reader** role; to toggle and change flags **Writer** (or a custom role limited to the projects and environments the agent may change). A service token is not tied to a person.
2. Copy the token (`api-...`, shown once) into `LAUNCHDARKLY_API_TOKEN` and run `launchdarkly_get_caller_identity` to check it.
3. On the EU instance or the federal one, change the connector base URL to `https://app.eu.launchdarkly.com` or `https://app.launchdarkly.us`.

**Workflow**
- Find things: `launchdarkly_list_projects`, `launchdarkly_get_project`, `launchdarkly_list_environments`, `launchdarkly_get_environment`; then `launchdarkly_list_flags` with `env: production` and `filter: query:checkout`, and `launchdarkly_get_flag` for its targeting.
- Is a flag still used: `launchdarkly_list_flag_statuses` and `launchdarkly_get_flag_status` (inactive or launched flags are candidates for clean-up).
- Release: `launchdarkly_create_flag`, then `launchdarkly_toggle_flag` per environment; change targeting or rollout with `launchdarkly_update_flag` (use `dry_run: true` to preview). Retire a flag with `archiveFlag` in `launchdarkly_update_flag`; `launchdarkly_delete_flag` removes it for good.
- Audiences: `launchdarkly_list_segments`, `launchdarkly_get_segment`, `launchdarkly_create_segment`, `launchdarkly_update_segment`.
- Experiments: `launchdarkly_list_metrics`, `launchdarkly_get_metric`, `launchdarkly_list_experiments`, `launchdarkly_get_experiment`.
- Who changed what: `launchdarkly_list_audit_log` (e.g. `spec: proj/default:env/production:flag/new-checkout`) and `launchdarkly_get_audit_log_entry`. People: `launchdarkly_list_members`, `launchdarkly_get_member`, `launchdarkly_list_teams`, `launchdarkly_get_team`.

**Switched off at install**: `launchdarkly_delete_flag`; it cannot be undone, so an admin switches it on when the team needs it.

**Before writing**: toggling a flag or changing its targeting in production changes what live users get within seconds. Confirm the project, environment and flag with the user first, and add a `comment` (some environments require one; approval-gated environments answer 405 and need an approval request in the app).

**Semantic patch**: `launchdarkly_toggle_flag`, `launchdarkly_update_flag` and `launchdarkly_update_segment` send instructions such as `{"kind": "addTargets", "contextKind": "user", "values": ["key-1"], "variationId": "<_id>"}`. Variation, rule and clause ids are the `_id` fields from `launchdarkly_get_flag` or `launchdarkly_get_segment`. Rollout weights are in thousandths of a percent (100000 = 100%).

**Reading the answers**: keys (project, environment, flag, segment) are what you pass on; member and audit log ids are 24-character hex strings. Dates are Unix milliseconds (`creationDate`, `lastModified`, `date`). In a flag, `environments.<key>.on` says whether targeting is on and `_summary.variations` what is served. Environment SDK and mobile keys are left out of the answers.

**Paging**: lists take `limit` and `offset` and return `totalCount` and `_links.next` while more pages exist. The audit log returns at most 20 entries; page back with `before` set to the `date` of the last entry.

**Errors**: 401 means a wrong or deleted token, 403 a token whose role does not allow the call, 404 an unknown key, 400 or 409 an invalid patch or a conflicting change (the message names the problem), 405 a change that needs approval, 429 the rate limit (wait for the time in `X-Ratelimit-Reset`).
prerequisites: A LaunchDarkly account and an access token (Organization settings, Authorization) with the Reader role, or Writer to change flags.

LAUNCHDARKLY_API_TOKEN.label: Access token
LAUNCHDARKLY_API_TOKEN.help: LaunchDarkly, Organization settings, Authorization, Create token: Reader role for reading, Writer (or a custom role) to change flags. Copy the api-... token.
LAUNCHDARKLY_API_TOKEN.patternMessage: Paste the access token starting with api-, without spaces. SDK keys (sdk-...) and mobile keys (mob-...) do not work here.

verifyHints.401: LaunchDarkly refused the token: it is wrong or was deleted. Create a new access token under Organization settings, Authorization.
verifyHints.403: The token works but its role does not allow this call. Give it the Writer role or a custom role with the needed actions.
verifyHints.429: LaunchDarkly rate-limited the token. Wait a moment and try again.

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_caller_identity
tools.description: Show what the access token is: account, token name and kind (personal or service), the member it belongs to and its scopes. Use it to check the token.

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_projects
tools.description: List the projects with key, name, tags and default client-side settings. Add `expand: environments` to include each project's environments (SDK keys are left out).

filter.description: Filters, comma-separated `field:value`, e.g. `query:mobile` (key or name contains) or `tags:core`.

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_project
tools.description: Get one project with its settings; add `expand: environments` for its environments (SDK keys are left out).

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_environments
tools.description: List the environments of a project (e.g. Production, Test) with key, name, colour, client-side id, approval and comment settings. SDK and mobile keys are left out.

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_environment
tools.description: Get one environment with its settings: client-side id, default TTL, secure mode, whether changes need comments, confirmation or approval, and its tags. SDK and mobile keys are left out.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_flags
tools.description: List the feature flags of a project: key, name, description, kind (boolean or multivariate), variations, tags, temporary flag, maintainer and creation date. With `env`, each flag also shows whether it is on in that environment and what it serves.

env.description: Environment key(s) whose state to include, e.g. `production`. Strongly recommended: without it the answer has no on or off state.

filter.description: Filters, comma-separated `field:value`: `query:checkout` (key or name contains), `tags:beta+web`, `state:live` (or deprecated, archived), `maintainerId:<member id>`, `hasExperiment:true`, `evaluated:{"after":<unix ms>},filterEnv:production`, `codeReferences.max:0`.

summary.description: true (default): leave out targeting rules and targets. false together with `env`: include the full targeting of that environment.

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_flag
tools.description: Get one feature flag with its variations (with their `_id`), defaults and, per environment, whether it is on, its targets, rules (with `_id`), fallthrough, off variation, prerequisites and version. Rule and variation ids are what `launchdarkly_update_flag` instructions need.

flag_key.description: Feature flag key (the key used in code), from `launchdarkly_list_flags`.

env.description: Only these environment keys (comma-separated) in `environments`, to keep the answer small.

expand.description: Extra fields, comma-separated: `evaluation` (context kinds evaluated in the last 30 days), `migrationSettings`.

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_flag_statuses
tools.description: List the evaluation status of every flag in one environment: new, active, inactive (not evaluated for 7 days) or launched (serving one variation to everyone), with the last time it was requested. Use it to find stale flags.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_flag_status
tools.description: Get the evaluation status of one flag in one environment (new, active, inactive, launched) and when it was last requested.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

flag_key.description: Feature flag key (the key used in code), from `launchdarkly_list_flags`.

tools.name: launchdarkly_create_flag
tools.description: Create a feature flag in a project, by default a boolean flag (variations true and false) that is off in every environment.

key.description: Flag key used in code, e.g. `new-checkout`. Letters, numbers, `.`, `_`, `-`.

temporary.description: true (default) for a release flag that will be removed; false for a permanent flag.

variations.description: Variations for a multivariate flag, each `{"value": ..., "name": "...", "description": "..."}`. Leave empty for a boolean flag.

defaults.description: Which variation (by index) new environments serve: `{"onVariation": 0, "offVariation": 1}`.

maintainer_id.description: Member id of the maintainer, from `launchdarkly_list_members` (default the token owner).

maintainer_team_key.description: Team key of the maintaining team, from `launchdarkly_list_teams`.

clone.description: Copy the full targeting of this existing flag key into the new flag.

tools.name: launchdarkly_toggle_flag
tools.description: Turn a feature flag on or off in one environment. Off serves the off variation to everyone; on applies the targeting. This changes what live users get immediately.

flag_key.description: Feature flag key (the key used in code), from `launchdarkly_list_flags`.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

comment.description: Why: shown in the audit log (required when the environment demands comments).

dry_run.description: Validate only and return the flag as it would be, without saving.

tools.name: launchdarkly_update_flag
tools.description: Change a feature flag with semantic patch instructions: targeting (addRule, removeRule, addClauses, addTargets, removeTargets, updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout, updateOffVariation, addPrerequisite), settings (updateName, updateDescription, addTags, removeTags, updateMaintainerMember, markTemporary, markPermanent) or lifecycle (deprecateFlag, archiveFlag, restoreFlag). Get rule and variation ids from `launchdarkly_get_flag` first.

flag_key.description: Feature flag key (the key used in code), from `launchdarkly_list_flags`.

environment_key.description: Environment key; required for targeting instructions, not for settings such as updateName or addTags.

instructions.description: Semantic patch instructions, each with `kind` and its parameters, e.g. [{"kind": "addTargets", "contextKind": "user", "values": ["user-key-1"], "variationId": "<variation _id>"}] or [{"kind": "updateFallthroughVariationOrRollout", "rolloutWeights": {"<variation _id>": 10000, "<other _id>": 90000}}] (weights in thousandths of a percent, total 100000).

comment.description: Why: shown in the audit log.

dry_run.description: Validate only and return the flag as it would be, without saving.

tools.name: launchdarkly_delete_flag
tools.description: Delete a feature flag from every environment of the project. SDKs then serve the fallback value from code. Prefer archiving it with `launchdarkly_update_flag` (`archiveFlag`), which can be restored.

flag_key.description: Feature flag key (the key used in code), from `launchdarkly_list_flags`.

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_segments
tools.description: List the segments of an environment: key, name, description, tags, whether it is a big segment, and when it changed.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_segment
tools.description: Get one segment with its included and excluded targets, rules (with `_id`) and version.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_create_segment
tools.description: Create an empty segment in one environment; add targets and rules afterwards with `launchdarkly_update_segment`.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

unbounded.description: true for a big segment (synced or imported lists of many contexts); false (default) for a standard segment.

tools.name: launchdarkly_update_segment
tools.description: Change a segment with semantic patch instructions: addIncludedTargets, removeIncludedTargets, addExcludedTargets, removeExcludedTargets, addRule, removeRule, addClauses, updateName, addTags and more.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

comment.description: Why: shown in the audit log.

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_metrics
tools.description: List the metrics of a project (conversions, clicks, page views, numeric custom events) with key, name, kind, event key, unit, success criteria and how many experiments use them.

filter.description: Filter expression with operators, e.g. `query equals "checkout"`, `tags contains ["revenue"]`, `eventKind equals custom`, `isNumeric equals true`, `metricUsedIn equals experiments`; join several with a comma.

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_metric
tools.description: Get one metric with its definition and, with `expand`, the experiments and metric groups that use it.

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_experiments
tools.description: List the experiments of a project across environments: key, name, hypothesis, environment, current iteration status (not started, running, stopped) and flag.

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_experiment
tools.description: Get one experiment with its hypothesis, current iteration (status, start date, treatments and traffic allocation, primary and secondary metrics) and flag.

environment_key.description: Environment key within the project, from `launchdarkly_list_environments` (e.g. `production`, `test`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_audit_log
tools.description: List audit log entries, newest first: who changed what (flags, segments, environments, members) and when, with the title, description and the resource. Filter by time, text, resource specifier and member.

before.description: Only entries before this time, Unix milliseconds.

after.description: Only entries after this time, Unix milliseconds.

q.description: Text to search for, e.g. a flag key or name.

member.description: Only changes by this member id, from `launchdarkly_list_members`.

limit.description: Entries to return, 1 to 20 (default 10). For older entries pass `before` = the date of the last entry.

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_audit_log_entry
tools.description: Get one audit log entry with the full change: the JSON patch or semantic instructions applied, the previous and current version of the resource and the comment.

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_members
tools.description: List the account members: id, email, name, role (reader, writer, admin, owner, no_access) or custom roles, teams, last seen and whether they verified their email.

filter.description: Filters, comma-separated `field:value`: `query:jane` (name or email), `role:admin|writer`, `team:platform`, `noteam:true`, `email:jane@example.com`, `lastSeen:{"before":<unix ms>}` or `lastSeen:{"never":true}`.

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_member
tools.description: Get one account member with role, custom roles, teams and permission grants.

member_id.description: Member id, from `launchdarkly_list_members` (or `me` for the token owner).

tools.name: launchdarkly_list_teams
tools.description: List the teams: key, name, description, member count and the roles they hold.

offset.description: Items to skip, for the next page: the previous offset plus limit (or follow `_links.next`).

tools.name: launchdarkly_get_team
tools.description: Get one team with its description and, with `expand`, members, roles, projects and maintainers.
